Inspect sources of observed-score variation

Source: R/api-plotting-multivariate-gstudy.R
plot.mfrm_multivariate_gstudy.Rd

Plot raw variance components for selected scores or one prespecified weighted score, or inspect the component covariance matrices. Then use mfrm_d_study() to assess how changing the measurement conditions affects G, Phi and SEM.

Usage 

# S3 method for class 'mfrm_multivariate_gstudy'
plot(
  x,
  score = NULL,
  weights = NULL,
  draw = TRUE,
  preset = "standard",
  type = c("components", "covariance"),
  ncol = NULL,
  intervals = FALSE,
  assumption = NULL,
  level = 0.95,
  method = "auto",
  draws = 20000L,
  seed = 20261016L,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

A result from mfrm_g_study().

score

Original score names in display order. Multiple scores produce separate component panels. The default selects the first score for type = "components", or all scores for type = "covariance". Do not supply both score and weights.

weights

Optional named numeric vector defining one composite. Name every score exactly once, with finite weights and at least one nonzero value. Names determine order. Signed weights permit difference scores; weights are not normalized. For a saved D-study, use its selected weight vector, for example plot(d$gstudy, weights = d$weights).

draw

Draw the figure; FALSE only returns its data.

preset

Plot style: "standard", "publication", "compact", or "monochrome". Omission uses the session plot default.

type

"components" for variance-component points, or "covariance" for one matrix heatmap per source. With intervals = TRUE, covariance instead displays one signed interval plot for exactly two selected scores. Covariance plots do not accept weights.

ncol

Positive number of panel columns. Defaults to at most two.

intervals

Logical; FALSE (default) shows point estimates. TRUE adds component confidence intervals in the same call; also specify assumption = "normal". Available for complete balanced ANOVA component plots, including supported nesting. Covariance intervals require an explicit method and exactly two scores. Explicit method = "reml_profile" also provides variance and two-score covariance intervals for identifiable incomplete sources, fitting a separate REML model while preserving the original points. method = "residual_contrast" uses retained ratings without likelihood fitting, but only Residual receives an interval. Other points remain visible with unavailable intervals and their reasons. Other methods use saved ANOVA summaries without refitting.

assumption

With intervals = TRUE, explicitly specify "normal" for independent normal random effects with constant component variances. This assumption is not tested.

level

Pointwise confidence level for intervals = TRUE, default 0.95.

method

Component interval method passed to confint.mfrm_multivariate_gstudy(). Single-score/composite variances use "auto" or "mls" for balanced ANOVA, or explicit experimental "reml_profile" for balanced/identifiable incomplete sources. Profile intervals have approximate calibration and no accompanying sampling SE. Covariance intervals require explicit "gci", "regression_region" or "reml_profile"; none is an automatic default. Explicit "residual_contrast" also supports incomplete sources for Residual only: exact normal-model variance limits or conservative covariance limits. It retains original points and a separate interval center without supplying the original estimator's sampling SE.

draws, seed

Numerical settings for covariance method = "gci". Defaults are 20000 pivotal draws and seed 20261016. See the confidence interval help for requirements and numerical endpoint bands.

...

Reserved; additional arguments are rejected.

Value

Invisibly, an mfrm_plot_data object with table (source, display label, selected estimate, sign status and full component-matrix PSD diagnostic), weights, score, kind, source_design, source_rows, axis labels and notes. plot, panels and ncol describe the view. Component tables include Score; covariance tables include Row, Column and Element (variance or covariance), with a shared fill_limits and heat_colors palette. With intervals, table also includes SE, Lower, Upper, RawLower, RawUpper, Level, Method, IntervalStatus and IntervalAvailable. intervals retains one complete confint() table per selected score or composite, with its assumptions and source context; unavailable_intervals retains rows without a drawable interval. Status still describes the sign of the point estimate. REML component tables additionally retain IntervalCenter, SEStatus, candidate bounds and Validation; full numerical profiles are retained in intervals. Saving the plot preserves them for as_ggplot() reuse. Covariance interval plots have kind = "Covariance", one forest panel, and the original pair in score. The full interval table retains covariance units, assumptions, numerical bands and SE/interval diagnostics. Save the result with saveRDS() for later as_ggplot() conversion, without recalculating intervals, or save the G-study to redraw it with base graphics.

Details

Each point is a variance-component estimate in squared score units. For weights \(w\), the component is \(w' \Sigma_s w\), including between-score covariances. Multiplying all weights by a constant multiplies each component by its square. Components describe the source model at the individual rating level; they have not been divided by future facet counts. They are not percentages, measurement-error shares for a future mean score, or MFRM severity estimates. A larger Person component describes greater person variation, not a defect in the assessment. A large rater component does not by itself identify which rater should receive feedback.

Negative estimates remain to the left of zero as open circles; nonnegative estimates use filled circles. An unconstrained negative estimate is not a negative population variance. Inspect the data/design and component diagnostics before interpreting it. No component is clipped, normalized or removed. A covariance matrix can be non-positive-semidefinite even when its projection for the selected score is positive; this is retained in the returned table and notes.

With intervals = TRUE, horizontal bars replace the stems from zero. They show the nonnegative-space intervals from confint.mfrm_multivariate_gstudy(): approximate Ting MLS intervals for components and chi-square intervals for the combined residual. They are pointwise, not simultaneous across components or scores. Negative point estimates can lie outside their nonnegative-space intervals. Square outlines mark estimates without an interval; consult IntervalStatus and unavailable_intervals for the reason. An empty interval or degenerate mean squares do not mean zero uncertainty. Raw endpoints, SEs and the full interval tables remain in the returned data. These intervals concern source variances, not future mean-score errors, G/Phi or off-diagonal covariance elements. With intervals = FALSE, stems run from zero to the estimate and do not represent uncertainty.

With method = "reml_profile", the bars instead show approximate restricted-likelihood component intervals. The points remain the original ANOVA/MINQUE estimates; the separate IntervalCenter is retained in the table. Profile SE and inapplicable MLS RawLower/RawUpper columns are NA; SEStatus explains this. Numerical availability does not establish coverage, especially near zero variances. The interval surrounds the REML center but does not enumerate remote disconnected accepted regions.

With method = "residual_contrast", only Residual receives a bar, based on a projection that removes all nonresidual effects. Points still show original ANOVA/MINQUE components; IntervalCenter records the projected residual estimate. No remaining residual degrees of freedom or numerically unresolved residual variation means unavailable limits. Exact variance coverage and conservative covariance coverage require the normal residual model at a fixed observed assignment; they do not extend to other sources or nonrandom omissions. See Residual contrasts in the interval help.

Multiple-score component panels share axes. Compare their magnitudes only when the score units are comparable. Covariance heatmaps show the selected submatrix for every source, with variances on the diagonal and covariances off the diagonal. Covariance units are the product of the two score units; these are not correlations. All panels share a color scale centered at zero and include signed numeric labels. Color presets use a diverging palette; "monochrome" uses a gray scale. Values are neither standardized nor converted to correlations. A negative covariance can be legitimate; a negative variance is an unconstrained estimate, not a population variance. ComponentPSD and returned notes describe the full source matrix even if only a subset of scores is shown. A large covariance alone does not diagnose halo. Cell labels are rounded for display; the table keeps exact values.

With type = "covariance", intervals = TRUE, select exactly two scores and an explicit method. A single horizontal interval plot across sources replaces the heatmaps. Covariance endpoints remain signed, including negative values. "gci" has approximate coverage and separate Monte Carlo endpoint bands; "regression_region" has conservative normal-model coverage but may be very wide. Square outlines retain unavailable intervals. SEStatus is separate: a one-df block can prevent an SE while still permitting a conservative interval. Open circles mark negative covariances, which can be legitimate. Explicit "reml_profile" instead fits a joint normal model, also for incomplete sources, and retains its separate IntervalCenter and full numerical diagnostics. Its chi-square calibration is experimental and can under-cover with few facet levels; no sampling SE is supplied. None of these methods is a correlation interval.

All estimated interactions are shown. The table preserves the original Source identifiers and adds a readable Label. For a crossed Person, Rater and Task design, the last label is "Person x Rater x Task + residual". Its Source remains Residual: with one observation per cell, the highest-order interaction and other residual variation cannot be estimated separately. A one-facet design instead shows "Person x Task + residual" (or the declared facet name); a nested design shows, for example, "Person x Rater(Task) + residual". No extra independent error component should be added to these combined estimates.

Measurement error is not synonymous with the component called Residual. For the supported random-facet mean-score projections, relative error includes the person-by-condition interactions and combined residual; absolute error additionally includes condition main effects and interactions without Person. The D-study divides each component by its applicable future counts, then adds these terms. Use plot(d, type = "sem") to view the square roots of the two error variances. Neither SEM nor a residual-component point is a sampling confidence interval. See mfrm_d_study() for the formulas and assumptions, and vignette("mfrmr-gtheory") for a worked source-to-error example.

This plot reads stored component estimates and preserves missing-data rules. Explicit REML intervals fit a separate model without replacing those points; other interval methods use the saved summaries. Titles and explanations are returned separately from the figure. Use plot_data(p, "notes") and keep them when sharing a figure. Both base R graphics and optional as_ggplot() conversion are supported.

See also

mfrm_g_study(), plot.mfrm_multivariate_d_study()

Examples 

tasks <- read.csv(system.file("extdata", "mgenova-table12.csv", package = "mfrmr"))
g <- mfrm_g_study(tasks, c("V", "W"), rater = NULL)
p <- plot(g, weights = c(V = .5, W = .5), preset = "monochrome",
          intervals = TRUE, assumption = "normal")

plot_data(p, "table")
#>     Source  Estimate ComponentPSD     Score Panel               Status
#> 1   Person 0.3438889         TRUE Composite     1 Nonnegative estimate
#> 2     Task 0.2120370         TRUE Composite     1 Nonnegative estimate
#> 3 Residual 1.0496296         TRUE Composite     1 Nonnegative estimate
#>                      Label        SE       Lower    Upper    RawLower RawUpper
#> 1                   Person 0.2241526 0.049657449 1.550716 0.049657449 1.550716
#> 2                     Task 0.1708214 0.006867325 1.798412 0.006867325 1.798412
#> 3 Person x Task + residual 0.2165221 0.722110052 1.665130 0.722110052 1.665130
#>   Level     Method IntervalStatus IntervalAvailable
#> 1  0.95   Ting MLS      Available              TRUE
#> 2  0.95   Ting MLS      Available              TRUE
#> 3  0.95 Chi-square      Available              TRUE
plot_data(p, "notes")
#>    Type
#> 1  note
#> 2  note

#> 4  note
#> 5  note
#> 6  note

Not future mean-score error contributions or percentages.
#> 2                                                                                                                                                                                                           Residual = Person x Task + residual: these sources cannot be separated with one observation per person-by-condition cell.
#> 3  Person variation is not measurement error. Relative error combines person-by-condition interactions and residual; absolute error also includes condition main effects and interactions without Person. Divide components by their applicable future counts before summing; use the D-study SEM plot for error in mean-score units.
#> 4                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Filled circles: nonnegative estimates; open circles: negative estimates. Weights are used as supplied.
#> 5                                                                                    Horizontal bars show nonnegative-space intervals: approximate Ting MLS for components; chi-square for the combined residual. They are not simultaneous across sources or scores. Negative points are retained even when outside those intervals.
#> 6                                                                                                                                                       Square outlines mark estimates without intervals; inspect IntervalStatus and unavailable_intervals. No bar does not mean zero uncertainty. Raw endpoints remain in the table.
#> 7                                                                                                                                                                      Pointwise normal-random-effects intervals for a prespecified score or fixed composite; MLS intervals are approximate. Not simultaneous or distribution robust.
#> 8                                                                                                                                                                                                 Estimates and SEs have squared score units. SE is sampling uncertainty in a component, not measurement SEM or uncertainty in G/Phi.
#> 9                                                                                                                                                                         Raw estimates and endpoints are retained. Lower/Upper intersect the interval with nonnegative variances; consult Status for empty or unavailable intervals.
#> 10                                                                                                                                                              Positive intervals whose width or endpoints cannot be represented remain unavailable with an explicit Status; a rounded zero width is not exact population knowledge.
#> 11                                                                                                                                                                                                            SE uses the df + 2 moment correction. Weights are used as supplied; saveRDS() preserves assumptions and source context.
#> 12                                                                                                                                                                                                               Compare magnitudes only for comparable score units. Shared plot scales do not make different score units equivalent.
plot(g, score = c("V", "W"))

covariance_plot <- plot(g, type = "covariance")

plot_data(covariance_plot, "table")
